extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners (accelerated examination context)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, required application elements, examiner practices, and procedural limits specific to applications granted special status under the USPTO Accelerated Examination program (including form-paragraph usage, timing rules, suspension/deferral, and sequence-submission requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic fees required on filing
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Basic filing fee, search fee, and examination fee, under 37 CFR 1.16 (see MPEP § 607 subsection I)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory fees must be included with the application on filing for it to be in condition for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application size fee when >100 sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) Application size fee under 37 CFR 1.16(s) (if the specification and drawings exceed 100 sheets of paper) (see MPEP § 607 subsection II)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay the application size fee when the spec + drawings exceed 100 sheets; see MPEP §607 II for calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executed oath or declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) An executed oath or declaration in compliance with 37 CFR 1.63
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oath/declaration must meet 37 CFR 1.63 requirements at filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification and claims compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: (4) A specification (in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52) containing a description (37 CFR 1.71) and claims in compliance with 37 CFR 1.75
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification must conform to formal requirements; claims must meet 37 CFR 1.75 formatting and content rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: (5) A title and an abstract in compliance with 37 CFR 1.72
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title and abstract must satisfy 37 CFR 1.72 to be acceptable on filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: (6) Drawings in compliance with 37 CFR 1.84
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If drawings are required, they must meet 37 CFR 1.84 standards (sizing, margins, views, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic sequence/table/listing submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: (7) Electronic submissions of sequence listings in compliance with 37 CFR 1.821(c) or (e), large tables, or computer listings in compliance with 37 CFR 1.96, submitted via the USPTO’s electronic filing system (EFS) in ASCII text as part of an associated file (if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listings, large tables or computer listings must be submitted electronically via EFS in ASCII as part of an associated file when applicable; follow cited CFRs for format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority claim identification
rubrics_metrics.description: (8) Foreign priority claim under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) identified in the executed oath or declaration or an application data sheet (if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign priority claims must be identified either in the oath/declaration or ADS at filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic benefit claim compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: (9) Domestic benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, or 365(c) in compliance with 37 CFR 1.78 (e.g., the specific reference to the prior application must be submitted in the first sentence(s) of the specification or in an application data sheet, and for any benefit claim to a non-English language provisional application, the application must include a statement that (a) an English language translation, and (b) a statement that the translation is accurate, have been filed in the provisional application) (if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefit claims must follow 37 CFR 1.78: cite the prior application in the first sentence(s) of the spec or ADS; if claiming benefit to a non-English provisional, include explicit translation and accuracy statements as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: English language translation and fee for non-English specs
rubrics_metrics.description: (10) English language translation under 37 CFR 1.52(d), a statement that the translation is accurate, and the processing fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i) (if the specification is in a non-English language)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the filing is not in English, include an English translation, an accuracy statement, and pay the processing fee per 1.17(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: No preliminary amendments on filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: (11) No preliminary amendments present on the filing date of the application
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary amendments should not be present on the declared filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: No petition for non‑signing inventor under 1.47
rubrics_metrics.description: (12) No petition under 37 CFR 1.47 for a non-signing inventor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At filing, there should be no outstanding petition under 1.47 regarding a non-signing inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design application additional compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is a design application, the application must also comply with the requirements set forth in 37 CFR 1.151, 1.152, 1.153, and 1.154.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design applications have separate filing/formality requirements per cited CFR sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide suggested classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should also provide a suggested classification, by class and subclass, for the application on the transmittal letter, petition, or an application data sheet as set forth in 37 CFR 1.76(b)(3)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing a suggested class/subclass on the transmittal letter/ADS expedites processing; this is a recommended practice (not a strict filing requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application must be in condition for examination on filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition to make special will be dismissed if the application omits an item or includes a paper that causes the Office of Initial Patent Examination (OIPE) to mail a notice during the formality review (e.g., notice of incomplete application, notice to file missing parts, notice to file corrected application papers, notice of omitted items, or notice of informal application). The opportunity to perfect a petition does not apply to applications that are not in condition for examination on filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application triggers any formality notice during OIPE review, a petition to make special will be dismissed. Being 'in condition for examination' on filing is required for special-status petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply to Office action must be fully responsive or bona fide attempt
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply to a non-final Office action is not fully responsive, but a bona fide attempt to advance the application to final action, the examiner may provide one month or thirty days, whichever is longer, for applicant to supply the omission or a fully responsive reply. No extensions of this time period under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will be permitted. Failure to timely file the omission or a fully responsive reply will result in abandonment of the application. If the reply is not a bona fide attempt or it is a reply to a final Office action, no additional time period will be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner discretion to grant a short corrective period (ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS whichever longer) applies only to bona fide, non-final replies; no 1.136 extensions allowed; missing the corrective period leads to abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: No withdrawal from special status via abandonment/continuation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no provision for “withdrawal” from special status under the accelerated examination program. An applicant may abandon the application that has been granted special status under the accelerated examination program in favor of a continuing application, and the continuing application will not be given special status under the accelerated examination program unless the continuing application is filed with a petition to make special under the accelerated examination program. The filing of an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114, however, will not result in an application being withdrawn from special status under the accelerated examination program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special status persists through filing an RCE; to transfer special status to a continuing application, you must file a new petition to make special with that continuing application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twelve‑month goal for final disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the accelerated examination program is to complete the examination of an application within twelve months from the filing date of the application. The twelve-month goal is achieved when one of the following final dispositions occurs: (1) the mailing of a notice of allowance; (2) the mailing of a final Office action; (3) the filing of an RCE; or (4) the abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a program objective only — the twelve‑month time frame may be extended by events (e.g., IDS citing new prior art after the mailing of a first Office action) and failures to meet the goal are neither petitionable nor appealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing of replies to preserve expedited processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any reply must be filed electronically via EFS-Web so that the papers will be expeditiously processed and considered. If the reply is not filed electronically via EFS-Web, the final disposition of the application may occur later than twelve months from the filing of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To maintain the program's expedited timing, file responses electronically through EFS-Web.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory period for replies in AE applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Since this application has been granted special status under the accelerated examination program, NO extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will be permitted. A shortened statutory period of ONE (1) MONTH or THIRTY (30) DAYS, whichever is longer, applies to certain requirements/communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AE applications get a shortened reply period (ONE MONTH or 30 DAYS whichever longer); 1.136 time extensions are barred for these periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph applicability and prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Many AE form paragraphs state: This form paragraph may only be used in an application filed on or after August 25, 2006, that has been granted special status under the accelerated examination program or other provisions under 37 CFR 1.102(c)(2) or (d). This form paragraph should not be used for an application that has been granted special status under 37 CFR 1.102(c)(1) on the basis of applicant’s health or age, or the Patent Prosecution Highway pilot program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs providing AE-specific text have strict applicability dates and special-status limits; examiners must ensure the application meets those prerequisites before using the AE form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph sequencing and cross‑references
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain form paragraphs must be preceded by specific other paragraphs or used only in particular contexts (e.g., 7.126.AE must be preceded by form paragraph 7.105 and should appear at the conclusion of any requirement for information mailed without any other Office action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the examiner notes about required preceding paragraphs and whether a paragraph is for initial vs subsequent communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE (37 CFR 1.114) eligibility constraints referenced in AE templates
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114, the application must be a utility or plant application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995. The RCE must be filed on or after May 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AE form paragraphs that acknowledge RCEs include these statutory/date constraints; examiners must confirm eligibility before using those templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling unsigned proposed replies
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed reply filed on [1] has not been entered because it is unsigned. Since the above-mentioned reply appears to be bona fide, applicant is given a TIME PERIOD of ONE (1) MONTH or THIRTY (30) DAYS from the mailing date of this notice... Examiner Note: Examiner should first try to contact applicant by telephone and ask for a properly signed reply or ratification of the reply. If attempts to contact applicant are unsuccessful, examiner may use this form paragraph in a letter requiring a properly signed reply or ratification if the reply is to a non-final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reply is unsigned, attempt phone contact to obtain signature/ratification; if unsuccessful, issue the ONE MONTH/30 DAY requirement letter per AE practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bona fide non‑responsive amendment practice limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of giving a short corrective period for bona fide non‑responsive amendments does not apply where there has been a deliberate omission of some necessary part of a complete reply, or where the application is subject to a final Office action. Under such cases, the examiner has no authority to grant an extension if the period for reply has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat deliberate omissions or replies to final actions as bona fide for the purpose of granting the short corrective period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canceled elected claims are non‑responsive
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment filed on [1] canceling all claims drawn to the elected invention and presenting only claims drawn to a non-elected invention is non-responsive (MPEP § 821.03). The remaining claims are not readable on the elected invention because [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment that removes all claims to the elected invention and leaves only non-elected claims renders the amendment non-responsive; provide an opportunity to correct if bona fide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for additional information (protest under 1.291)
rubrics_metrics.description: The protest under 37 CFR 1.291 filed on [1] has been considered. In order to reach a full and proper consideration of the issues raised therein, it is necessary to obtain additional information from applicant regarding these issues. In particular [2]. The failure to reply to this requirement for information within ONE (1) MONTH or THIRTY (30) DAYS, whichever is longer, of the mailing date of this requirement will result in abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific additional information requested must be provided within the ONE MONTH/30 DAYS shortened period; failure to respond results in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence rules non‑compliance leads to abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: This application contains sequence disclosures... However, this application fails to comply with the requirements of 37 CFR 1.821 through 1.825 for the reason(s) set forth below... Applicant is given ONE (1) MONTH, or THIRTY (30) DAYS, whichever is longer... Failure to comply with these requirements will result in ABANDONMENT of the application under 37 CFR 1.821(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-compliance with sequence listing rules (37 CFR 1.821-1.825) in AE applications triggers a ONE MONTH/30 DAY cure period; failure to cure results in abandonment under 1.821(g). Attach Notice To Comply and marked-up Raw Sequence Listing when mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRF diskette/compact disc submission problem practice
rubrics_metrics.description: When a computer readable form (CRF) of the sequence listing was submitted but the CRF could not be processed, the applicant is given ONE (1) MONTH, or THIRTY (30) DAYS... Failure to comply will result in ABANDONMENT of the application under 37 CFR 1.821(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the CRF Diskette Problem Report procedures; request return of the report with the reply; initial vs subsequent communication rules apply (use 24.03/24.04 for subsequent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact disc/CRF submission not fully responsive — bona fide attempt rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The reply filed [1] is not fully responsive to the Office communication mailed [2] for the reason(s) set forth below... Since the above-mentioned reply appears to be bona fide, applicant is given a TIME PERIOD of ONE (1) MONTH or THIRTY (30) DAYS from the mailing date of this notice... This practice does not apply where there has been a deliberate omission... or where the reason the reply is incomplete cannot be characterized as an apparent oversight or apparent inadvertence. Under such cases the examiner has no authority to grant an extension if the six‑month period for reply has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this practice for bona fide incomplete CD/CRF replies; if the six‑month reply window has expired or omission appears deliberate, use form paragraph 24.04 and do not grant the short period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of action (37 CFR 1.103) — general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: On request of the applicant, the Office may grant a suspension of action by the Office under this paragraph for good and sufficient cause. The Office will not suspend action if a reply by applicant to an Office action is outstanding. Any petition for suspension of action under this paragraph must specify a period of suspension not exceeding six months. Any petition for suspension of action under this paragraph must also include: (1) A showing of good and sufficient cause for suspension of action; and (2) The fee set forth in § 1.17(g), unless such cause is the fault of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension under 1.103(a) applies to action by the Office (examiner); it cannot be used when an applicant has an outstanding Office action awaiting reply. Petitions must be separate papers, include the petition fee, and request a specific reasonable suspension <=6 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited suspensions for CPA and RCE (1.103(b),(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited suspension of action in a continued prosecution application (CPA) filed under § 1.53(d) — period not exceeding three months; request must be filed with CPA and include processing fee 1.17(i). Limited suspension after filing an RCE under § 1.114 — period not exceeding three months; request must be filed with the RCE and include processing fee 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPA and RCE suspensions are short (<=3 months) and require the processing fee under 1.17(i); note CPA practice limitations for utility and plant apps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of examination (1.103(d)) — conditions and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: On request of the applicant, the Office may grant a deferral of examination... for a period not extending beyond three years from the earliest filing date for which a benefit is claimed under title 35... A request for deferral of examination under this paragraph must include the publication fee set forth in § 1.18(d) and the processing fee set forth in § 1.17(i). A request for deferral of examination under this paragraph will not be granted unless: (1) [the application is an international application entering the national stage after compliance with § 1.495]; (2) The applicant has not filed a nonpublication request under § 1.213(a), or has filed a request under § 1.213(b) to rescind a previously filed nonpublication request; (3) The application is in condition for publication as provided in § 1.211(c); and (4) The Office has not issued either an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferral is limited to a maximum of three years and requires payment of publication and processing fees; multiple substantive eligibility conditions must be met (national-stage/international application status, no nonpublication request, application publishable, and no prior Office action/notice of allowance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension reduces patent term adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(a)-(d) at the applicant’s request will cause a reduction in patent term adjustment accumulated (if any) under 37 CFR 1.703. The reduction is equal to the number of days beginning on the date a request for suspension of action was filed and ending on the date of the termination of the suspension. See 37 CFR 1.704(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that voluntary suspension requests subtract from any accumulated PTA; quantify reduction as days of suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension vs extension distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension of action (37 CFR 1.103) should not be confused with extension of time for reply (37 CFR 1.136). It is to be noted that a suspension of action applies to an impending Office action by the examiner whereas an extension of time for reply applies to action by the applicant. In other words, the action cannot be suspended in an application which contains an outstanding Office action or requirement awaiting reply by the applicant. It is only the action by the examiner which can be suspended under 37 CFR 1.103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 1.103 for suspending examiner action; use 1.136 to extend applicant reply times. They are distinct remedies with different impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition presentation requirements under 1.103(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(a) must: (A) be presented as a separate paper; (B) be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(g); (C) request a specific and reasonable period of suspension not greater than 6 months; and (D) present good and sufficient reasons why the suspension is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet these formal petition requirements will likely result in denial and the application being taken up for action in due course.
